question: Which of the following anti-tubercular drug is avoided in a HIV positive patient on zidovudine, lamivudine and indinavir therapy who develops TB?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "HIV positive patient" -> "on zidovudine, lamivudine, and indinavir" -> "develops TB" -> "need for anti-tubercular therapy" -> "Rifampicin interacts with zidovudine" -> "potentially reduces efficacy of zidovudine" -> "Rifampicin is avoided" -> 85%

CHAIN: "HIV positive patient" -> "on antiretroviral therapy" -> "develops TB" -> "consideration of anti-tubercular drugs" -> "Rifampicin is a potent inducer" -> "induces metabolism of zidovudine" -> "may lead to subtherapeutic levels of zidovudine" -> "Rifampicin is avoided" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient with TB" -> "HIV positive" -> "on zidovudine, lamivudine, indinavir" -> "Rifampicin is a first-line TB drug" -> "Rifampicin can cause drug interactions" -> "specifically with zidovudine" -> "risk of reduced antiviral efficacy" -> "Rifampicin is avoided" -> 80%

CHAIN: "HIV positive patient" -> "receiving ART" -> "develops TB" -> "needs anti-tubercular treatment" -> "Rifampicin is contraindicated" -> "due to interactions with ART" -> "increased risk of treatment failure" -> "Rifampicin is avoided" -> 90%
analysis: Rifampicin is known to induce the metabolism of many drugs by inducing cytochrome P450 enzymes, which can significantly reduce the effectiveness of antiretroviral drugs such as zidovudine and lamivudine. Therefore, it is avoided in HIV positive patients on these therapies who develop TB.
